claim: Cellular senescence is a contributor to intervertebral disc (IVD) degeneration and low back pain.
source: Cellular senescence is a contributor to intervertebral disc (IVD) degeneration and low back pain.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a foundational premise for the study, supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: RG-7112 selectively kills senescent IVD cells through apoptosis.
source: Here, we found that RG-7112, a potent mouse double-minute two protein inhibitor, selectively kills senescent IVD cells through apoptosis.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing increased caspase-3 activity and decreased p16Ink4a-positive cells following RG-7112 treatment.

claim: Both RG-7112 and o-Vanillin affect a functional gene network related to cell death and survival.
source: Gene expression pathway analysis was used to compare the functional networks of genes affected by RG-7112, a pure synthetic senolytic with o-Vanillin a natural and anti-inflammatory senolytic. Both affected a functional gene network related to cell death and survival.
evidence: This is supported by gene expression analysis and IPA pathway analysis showing networks related to cell death and survival.

claim: O-Vanillin affects networks related to cell cycle progression as well as connective tissue development and function.
source: O-Vanillin also affected networks related to cell cycle progression as well as connective tissue development and function.
evidence: This is supported by IPA analysis showing multiple networks affected by o-Vanillin treatment.

claim: Both senolytics effectively decreased the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) of IVD cells.
source: Both senolytics effectively decreased the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) of IVD cells.
evidence: This is supported by cytokine array and Luminex assay data showing decreased levels of multiple SASP factors.

claim: A single dose of senolytics improved disc matrix homeostasis in degenerating intact human discs.
source: Furthermore, bioavailability and efficacy were verified ex vivo in the physiological environment of degenerating intact human discs where a single dose improved disc matrix homeostasis.
evidence: This is supported by T1ρ MRI data showing increased signal intensity and safranin-O staining showing increased proteoglycan content.

claim: Matrix improvement correlated with a reduction in senescent cells and SASP.
source: Matrix improvement correlated with a reduction in senescent cells and SASP, supporting a translational potential of targeting senescent cells as a therapeutic intervention.
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry showing decreased p16Ink4a-positive cells and Luminex data showing decreased SASP factors in treated discs.

claim: Low back pain is experienced by ~80% of individuals at some point in their lifetime.
source: Low back pain is a global health problem that is experienced by ~80% of individuals at some point in their lifetime (Vos et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Vos et al., 2012.

claim: Low back pain is the number one single cause of years lived with disability.
source: This problem is the number one single cause of years lived with disability with enormous personal and health system related costs (Institute of Medicine (US) Committee on Advancing Pain Research, Care, and Education, 2016; Hartvigsen et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Institute of Medicine (US) Committee on Advancing Pain Research, Care, and Education, 2016 and Hartvigsen et al., 2018.

claim: Intervertebral disc (IVD) degeneration is a major factor contributing to low back pain.
source: Intervertebral disc (IVD) degeneration is a major factor contributing to low back pain (Vos et al., 2012; Adams and Hutton, 1983; Vergroesen et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Vos et al., 2012; Adams and Hutton, 1983; Vergroesen et al., 2015.

claim: Cellular senescence is a state of irreversible growth arrest occurring in response to cellular stress.
source: One novel approach to treat painful degeneration is to target cellular senescence, a state of irreversible growth arrest occurring in response to cellular stress (Tchkonia et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Tchkonia et al., 2013 and represents established scientific knowledge.

claim: Stress-induced premature senescence is caused by factors such as oxidative and genotoxic stresses.
source: Stress-induced premature senescence is caused by factors such as oxidative and genotoxic stresses (Toussaint et al., 2000; Campisi and d'Adda di Fagagna, 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Toussaint et al., 2000 and Campisi and d'Adda di Fagagna, 2007.

claim: Accumulation of senescent cells during tissue degeneration contributes directly to initiation and development of osteoarthritis.
source: Increasing evidence suggests that accumulation of senescent cells during tissue degeneration contributes directly to initiation and development of musculoskeletal degenerative diseases like osteoarthritis (Jeon et al., 2017) and IVD degeneration (Le Maitre et al., 2007; Feng et al., 2016; Wang et al., 2016; Patil et al., 2018; Cherif et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Jeon et al., 2017.

claim: Accumulation of senescent cells during tissue degeneration contributes directly to initiation and development of IVD degeneration.
source: Increasing evidence suggests that accumulation of senescent cells during tissue degeneration contributes directly to initiation and development of musculoskeletal degenerative diseases like osteoarthritis (Jeon et al., 2017) and IVD degeneration (Le Maitre et al., 2007; Feng et al., 2016; Wang et al., 2016; Patil et al., 2018; Cherif et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Le Maitre et al., 2007; Feng et al., 2016; Wang et al., 2016; Patil et al., 2018; Cherif et al., 2019.

claim: Senescent cells secrete a range of cytokines, chemokines, growth factors, and proteases termed as the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP).
source: Senescent cells secrete a range of cytokines, chemokines, growth factors, and proteases termed as the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) (Herbig et al., 2006; Kuilman et al., 2008; Coppé et al., 2008; Xu et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Herbig et al., 2006; Kuilman et al., 2008; Coppé et al., 2008; Xu et al., 2015.

claim: SASP factors are suggested to further induce senescence in a paracrine manner.
source: These SASP factors are suggested to further induce senescence in a paracrine manner (Acosta et al., 2013), to promote matrix catabolism and sterile inflammation in IVDs, thereby accelerating the degenerative process (Parrinello et al., 2005; Tominaga, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Acosta et al., 2013.

claim: SASP factors promote matrix catabolism and sterile inflammation in IVDs, thereby accelerating the degenerative process.
source: These SASP factors are suggested to further induce senescence in a paracrine manner (Acosta et al., 2013), to promote matrix catabolism and sterile inflammation in IVDs, thereby accelerating the degenerative process (Parrinello et al., 2005; Tominaga, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Parrinello et al., 2005 and Tominaga, 2015.

claim: Elimination of senescent cells enhances disc tissue homeostasis in genetically modified progeroid Ercc1−/Δ22 mice.
source: Elimination of senescent cells enhances disc tissue homeostasis in genetically modified progeroid Ercc1−/Δ22 and p16‐3MR (Patil et al., 2019) mice suggesting that senotherapeutic drugs have great potential to treat low back pain resulting from IVD degeneration.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Patil et al., 2019.

claim: Elimination of senescent cells enhances disc tissue homeostasis in genetically modified p16‐3MR mice.
source: Elimination of senescent cells enhances disc tissue homeostasis in genetically modified progeroid Ercc1−/Δ22 and p16‐3MR (Patil et al., 2019) mice suggesting that senotherapeutic drugs have great potential to treat low back pain resulting from IVD degeneration.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Patil et al., 2019.

claim: RG-7112 is a highly potent and selective MDM2 antagonist.
source: The FDA-approved drug RG-7112 (RO5045337) (Weber, 2010; Laberge et al., 2018) is a highly potent and selective MDM2 antagonist (Weber, 2010; Tovar et al., 2013) that restores the physiological activity of p53.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Weber, 2010 and Tovar et al., 2013.

claim: RG-7112 restores the physiological activity of p53.
source: The FDA-approved drug RG-7112 (RO5045337) (Weber, 2010; Laberge et al., 2018) is a highly potent and selective MDM2 antagonist (Weber, 2010; Tovar et al., 2013) that restores the physiological activity of p53.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Weber, 2010 and Tovar et al., 2013.

claim: RG-7112 is the first nutlin family member to be assessed clinically.
source: RG-7112 is the first nutlin family member to be assessed clinically (Weber, 2010; Laberge et al., 2018) showing evidence of acceptable safety (Ray-Coquard et al., 2012; Constantinidou et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Weber, 2010 and Laberge et al., 2018.

claim: RG-7112 shows evidence of acceptable safety in clinical trials.
source: RG-7112 is the first nutlin family member to be assessed clinically (Weber, 2010; Laberge et al., 2018) showing evidence of acceptable safety (Ray-Coquard et al., 2012; Constantinidou et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Ray-Coquard et al., 2012 and Constantinidou et al., 2012.

claim: RG-7112 selectively kills senescent lung fibroblasts (IMR90) where senescence was induced by ionizing radiation (IR).
source: RG-7112 was reported to selectively kill senescent lung fibroblasts (IMR90) where senescence was induced by ionizing radiation (IR) (Weber, 2010; Laberge et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Weber, 2010 and Laberge et al., 2018.

claim: o-Vanillin is known for its antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects.
source: The natural compound o-Vanillin, known for its antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects (Santosh Kumar et al., 2002; Oliveira et al., 2014; Shah et al., 2019; Marton et al., 2016), has recently been described for its senotherapeutic activity in human IVD cells (Cherif et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Santosh Kumar et al., 2002; Oliveira et al., 2014; Shah et al., 2019; Marton et al., 2016.

claim: o-Vanillin has senotherapeutic activity in human IVD cells.
source: The natural compound o-Vanillin, known for its antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects (Santosh Kumar et al., 2002; Oliveira et al., 2014; Shah et al., 2019; Marton et al., 2016), has recently been described for its senotherapeutic activity in human IVD cells (Cherif et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Cherif et al., 2019.

claim: There are currently no large bipedal animal models that mimic naturally occurring IVD degeneration and human genetic background.
source: One caveat in the field is that there are currently no large bipedal animal models that mimic naturally occurring IVD degeneration and human genetic background (Alini et al., 2008; Jin et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Alini et al., 2008 and Jin et al., 2018.

claim: RG-7112 significantly decreased the percentage of p16Ink4a positive NP cells (11.48%; p<0.001) compared to untreated control cultures.
source: RG-7112 significantly decreased the percentage of p16Ink4a positive NP (11.48%; p<0.001) and AF (20.03%; p<0.0001) cells compared to untreated control cultures (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: RG-7112 significantly decreased the percentage of p16Ink4a positive AF cells (20.03%; p<0.0001) compared to untreated control cultures.
source: RG-7112 significantly decreased the percentage of p16Ink4a positive NP (11.48%; p<0.001) and AF (20.03%; p<0.0001) cells compared to untreated control cultures (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: RG-7112 significantly increased the percentage of Ki-67-positive NP cells (23.07%; p<0.05).
source: Similarly, RG-7112 significantly increased the percentage of Ki-67-positive NP (23.07%; p<0.05) and AF (34.92%; p<0.0001) cells (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: RG-7112 significantly increased the percentage of Ki-67-positive AF cells (34.92%; p<0.0001).
source: Similarly, RG-7112 significantly increased the percentage of Ki-67-positive NP (23.07%; p<0.05) and AF (34.92%; p<0.0001) cells (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Caspase-3-positive AF cells increased significantly (17.88%; p<0.01) following RG-7112 treatment.
source: Caspase-3-positive AF cells increased significantly (17.88%; p<0.01) while a non-significant increase (2.94%; p=0.51) was observed in NP cells following treatment (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: A non-significant increase in caspase-3-positive NP cells (2.94%; p=0.51) was observed following RG-7112 treatment.
source: Caspase-3-positive AF cells increased significantly (17.88%; p<0.01) while a non-significant increase (2.94%; p=0.51) was observed in NP cells following treatment (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Both NP (9.87%; p<0.05) and AF (11.87%; p<0.05) cells showed a significant increase in metabolic activity following RG-7112 treatment.
source: No cytotoxicity was observed following treatment. In contrast, both NP (9.87%; p<0.05) and AF (11.87%; p<0.05) cells showed a significant increase in metabolic activity (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by metabolic activity assay data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: A significant increase in proteoglycan release in conditioned media was observed after 14 days of RG-7112 treatment.
source: Finally, we investigated proteoglycan synthesis using the DMMB assay following treatment. A significant increase in proteoglycan release in conditioned media was observed after 14 days of treatment (Figure 1 —figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is supported by DMMB assay data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1G.

claim: Compared with the control group, the number of differentially expressed genes for o-Vanillin were 40 (30 upregulated and 10 downregulated).
source: Compared with the control group, the number of differentially expressed genes for o-Vanillin were 40 (30 upregulated and 10 downregulated) and eight for RG-7112 (6 upregulated and two downregulated).
evidence: This is supported by gene expression analysis data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Compared with the control group, the number of differentially expressed genes for RG-7112 were eight (6 upregulated and two downregulated).
source: Compared with the control group, the number of differentially expressed genes for o-Vanillin were 40 (30 upregulated and 10 downregulated) and eight for RG-7112 (6 upregulated and two downregulated).
evidence: This is supported by gene expression analysis data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Three genes are commonly upregulated by both RG-7112 and o-Vanillin: MAPK14, CDC25c and CDKN2D (p19ARF).
source: In upregulated DEGs, three are common to both drugs, mitogen-activated protein kinase 14 (MAPK14), cell division cycle 25 c (CDC25c) and cyclin dependant kinase 2D (CDKN2D or p19ARF).
evidence: This is supported by gene expression analysis data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: No down-regulated DEGs were common to RG-7112 and o-Vanillin.
source: No down-regulated DEGs were common to the drugs.
evidence: This is supported by gene expression analysis data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: CCNB1 is upregulated by RG-7112 and downregulated by o-Vanillin.
source: Although cyclin B1 (CCNB1) is significantly expressed following the treatment with the two compounds, it is upregulated in RG-7112 and downregulated in o-Vanillin (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by gene expression analysis data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Cell cycle and senescence genes were significantly downregulated by o-Vanillin including CDK2A (p16Ink4a), p18ARF, Cyclin A2, CCNB1, CDC25c, Vimentin, MAPK6 and CHEK1.
source: Cell cycle and senescence genes were significantly downregulated including cyclin dependent kinase 2A (CDK2A or p16Ink4a), cyclin dependent kinase 2C (p18ARF), Cyclin A2, CCNB1, CDC25c, Vimentin, Mitogen-activated protein kinase 6 (MAPK6) and Checkpoint kinase 1(CHEK1) (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by gene expression analysis data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Apoptotic and proliferative genes significantly upregulated by o-Vanillin include Bcl-2, Bcl-2-like 1, Bcl-2-like 2, IRF5, IRF7 and ERBB2.
source: Examples of apoptotic and proliferative genes significantly upregulated by o-Vanillin include B-cell lymphoma 2 (Bcl-2), Bcl-2-like 1, Bcl-2-like 2, interferon regulatory factor 5 (IRF5), IRF7 and receptor tyrosine-protein kinase ERBB2.
evidence: This is supported by gene expression analysis data shown in Figure 2.

claim: RG-7112 treatment significantly reduced the levels of INF-γ, IL-6, IL-8 and CCL24 in pellet culture media.
source: The levels of INF-γ, IL-6, IL-8 and CCL24 were significantly decreased following both treatments whereas the decrease in CCL7, CXCL1, CXCL5, CXCL9, CXCL10 and VEGF significance was reached only following o-Vanillin treatment (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by Luminex assay data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: o-Vanillin treatment significantly reduced the levels of INF-γ, IL-6, IL-8, CCL24, CCL7, CXCL1, CXCL5, CXCL9, CXCL10 and VEGF in pellet culture media.
source: The levels of INF-γ, IL-6, IL-8 and CCL24 were significantly decreased following both treatments whereas the decrease in CCL7, CXCL1, CXCL5, CXCL9, CXCL10 and VEGF significance was reached only following o-Vanillin treatment (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by Luminex assay data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Increased T1ρ values were found in RG-7112 and o-Vanillin-treated discs while vehicle-treated discs displayed decreased T1ρ values.
source: Increased T1ρ values were found in RG-7112 and o-Vanillin-treated discs while vehicle-treated discs displayed decreased T1ρ values. (Figure 4B (a-d))
evidence: This is supported by MRI data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Vehicle-treated control IVDs showed a non-significant decrease of 13.2 ± 4.7% (p=0.058) in T1ρ values post-treatment.
source: Quantification of pre- versus post- treatment intensity values showed a non-significant decrease of 13.2 ± 4.7% (p=0.058) in vehicle-treated control IVDs.
evidence: This is supported by MRI quantification data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: RG-7112 treated discs showed a significant 6.8 ± 1.5% (p=0.024) increase in the T1ρ value post-treatment.
source: In RG-7112 treated discs, there was a significant 6.8 ± 1.5% (p=0.024) increase in the T1ρ value post-treatment.
evidence: This is supported by MRI quantification data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: o-Vanillin treated discs displayed a significant increase of 11.1 ± 1.2% (p=0.001) in T1ρ values following treatment.
source: Discs that were treated with o-Vanillin, displayed a significant increase of 11.1 ± 1.2% (p=0.001) in T1ρ values following treatment (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by MRI quantification data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: RG-7112 treatment showed a significant decrease in the number of senescent cells of 17.38 ± 1.6% (p=0.0017) in intact IVDs compared with vehicle-treated control discs.
source: Indeed, immunohistochemical assessment of p16Ink4a showed a significant decrease in the number of senescent cells of 17.38 ± 1.6% (p=0.0017) in RG-7112 and 22.65 ± 3.6% (p=0.008) in o-Vanillin-treated IVDs compared with vehicle-treated control discs (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: o-Vanillin treatment showed a significant decrease in the number of senescent cells of 22.65 ± 3.6% (p=0.008) in intact IVDs compared with vehicle-treated control discs.
source: Indeed, immunohistochemical assessment of p16Ink4a showed a significant decrease in the number of senescent cells of 17.38 ± 1.6% (p=0.0017) in RG-7112 and 22.65 ± 3.6% (p=0.008) in o-Vanillin-treated IVDs compared with vehicle-treated control discs (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Quantification of Ki-67 staining showed a non-significant increase in both RG-7112 and o-Vanillin 3.05 ± 3.4% (p=0.4) treated IVDs.
source: Quantification of Ki-67 staining showed a non-significant increase in both RG-7112 and o-Vanillin 3.05 ± 3.4% (p=0.4) treated IVDs (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: A single injection with RG-7112 strongly decreased secretion of IL-7 (−60.63% (p=0.01)), IL-6 (−59.39% (p=0.14)), CXCL1 (−36.72% (p=0.26)), GRO-abg (−32.84% (p=0.21)) and CCL24 (−30.57% (p=0.15)) in intact disc culture media.
source: Interestingly, a single injection with RG-7112 strongly decreased secretion of several proinflammatory cytokines and chemokines including IL-7 (−60.63% (p=0.01)), IL-6 (−59.39% (p=0.14)), CXCL1 (−36.72% (p=0.26)), GRO-abg (−32.84% (p=0.21)) and CCL24 (−30.57% (p=0.15)).
evidence: This is supported by cytokine array data shown in Figure 5A.
This is supported by cytokine array data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Both RG-7112 and o-Vanillin significantly decreased IL-8 by 18.72% (p=0.004) and 11.75% (p=0.04) respectively in intact disc culture media.
source: Both compounds significantly decreased IL-8 by 18.72% (p=0.004) for RG-7112 and by 11.75% (p=0.04) for o-Vanillin.
evidence: This is supported by cytokine array data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: RG-7112 significantly reduced the concentrations of TNF-α (mean 12.4 pg/ml in pre, 6.8 pg/ml in post, p=0.03), CCL11 (mean 13.1 pg/ml in pre, 7.8 pg/ml in post, p=0.009), CCL24 (mean 201.7 pg/ml in pre, 101.1 pg/ml in post, p=0.04), CXCL1 (mean 261.8 pg/ml in pre, 148.2 pg/ml in post, p=0.001), CXCL10 (mean 197.1 pg/ml in pre, 158.7 pg/ml in post, p=0.04) and Angiogenin (mean 51.7 pg/ml in pre, 37.6 pg/ml in post, p=0.02) in intact disc culture media.
source: For RG-7112, these proteins were TNF-α (mean 12.4 pg/ml in pre, 6.8 pg/ml in post, p=0.03), CCL11 (mean 13.1 pg/ml in pre, 7.8 pg/ml in post, p=0.009), CCL24 (mean 201.7 pg/ml in pre, 101.1 pg/ml in post, p=0.04), CXCL1 (mean 261.8 pg/ml in pre, 148.2 pg/ml in post, p=0.001), CXCL10 (mean 197.1 pg/ml in pre, 158.7 pg/ml in post, p=0.04) and Angiogenin (mean 51.7 pg/ml in pre, 37.6 pg/ml in post, p=0.02).
evidence: This is supported by Luminex assay data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: o-Vanillin significantly reduced the levels of INF-γ (mean 1.6 pg/ml in pre, 1.1 pg/ml in post, p=0.04), CCL24 (mean 232.7 pg/ml in pre, 73.7 pg/ml in post, p=0.02), CXCL1 (mean 313.9 pg/ml in pre, 130.2 pg/ml in post, p=0.01), Angiogenin (mean 47.4 pg/ml in pre, 35.5 pg/ml in post, p=0.02) and VEGF-A (mean 24802.1 pg/ml in pre, 20905.5 pg/ml in post, p=0.04) in intact disc culture media.
source: o-Vanillin significantly reduced the levels of INF-γ (mean 1.6 pg/ml in pre, 1.1 pg/ml in post, p=0.04), CCL24 (mean 232.7 pg/ml in pre, 73.7 pg/ml in post, p=0.02), CXCL1 (mean 313.9 pg/ml in pre, 130.2 pg/ml in post, p=0.01), Angiogenin (mean 47.4 pg/ml in pre, 35.5 pg/ml in post, p=0.02) and VEGF-A (mean 24802.1 pg/ml in pre, 20905.5 pg/ml in post, p=0.04) (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is supported by Luminex assay data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: A significant increase in the release of four factors was found in vehicle treated discs: INF-γ (mean 1 pg/ml in pre, 1.45 pg/ml in post, p=0.02), CCL11 (mean 7 pg/ml in pre, 19.2 pg/ml in post, p=0.04), CXCL1 (mean 104.3 pg/ml in pre, 476.9 pg/ml in post, p=0.03) and CXCL9 (mean 60.4 pg/ml in pre, 162.4 pg/ml in post, p=0.01).
source: Finally, we found a significant increase in the release of four factors in vehicle treated discs: INF-γ (mean 1 pg/ml in pre, 1.45 pg/ml in post, p=0.02), CCL11 (mean 7 pg/ml in pre, 19.2 pg/ml in post, p=0.04), CXCL1 (mean 104.3 pg/ml in pre, 476.9 pg/ml in post, p=0.03) and CXCL9 (mean 60.4 pg/ml in pre, 162.4 pg/ml in post, p=0.01).
evidence: This is supported by Luminex assay data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: RG-7112 has a potent senotherapeutic and a strong proliferative effect on human IVD cells in vitro.
source: Here, we demonstrated that RG-7112 has a potent senotherapeutic and a strong proliferative effect on human IVD cells in vitro.
evidence: This is supported by data showing decreased p16Ink4a-positive cells and increased Ki-67-positive cells.

claim: Metabolic activity and extracellular matrix production were increased in RG-7112 treated cultures.
source: Metabolic activity and extracellular matrix production were also increased in treated cultures.
evidence: This is supported by Alamar blue assay and DMMB assay data.

claim: RG-7112 treatment specifically targets senescent cells by activating the caspase-3 apoptotic pathway.
source: We verified that treatment specifically targets senescent cells by activating the caspase-3 apoptotic pathway.
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry and caspase-3/7 activity assay data.

claim: UBX0101 triggers apoptosis of senescent chondrocytes in a murine osteoarthritis model.
source: This is similar to the effect of UBX0101, an analogue of RG-7112 that triggers apoptosis of senescent chondrocytes in a murine osteoarthritis model (Jeon et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Jeon et al., 2017.

claim: Phase I and II clinical trials are in progress to assess safety, tolerability and clinical effects of single dose of intra-articular administration of UBX0101 in patients with moderate to severe painful knee osteoarthritis.
source: Currently, phase I and II clinical trials are in progress to assess safety, tolerability and clinical effects of single dose (NCT03513016 and NCT04129944) and both single and repeated doses (NCT04229225) of intra-articular administration of UBX0101 in patients with moderate to severe painful knee osteoarthritis (van Deursen, 2014; Vassilev et al., 2004; Vu et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to clinical trial identifiers and references.

claim: RG-7112 decreased gene expression of CDK1A and MDM2 and increased expression of E2F1, RB factors, MAPK-14, CDK2D, CCNB1 and CDC25c.
source: RG-7112 decreased gene expression of CDK1A and MDM2 and increased expression of the E2F1, RB factors, MAPK-14, CDK2D, CCNB1 and CDC25c.
evidence: This is supported by gene expression analysis data shown in Figure 2.

claim: o-Vanillin modulated gene expression of 40 genes including upregulation of CDK6, CDK2C, CDK2D, and CDC25c while expression levels of CDK2A, Cyclin A2, Cyclin D1 and CCNB1 were decreased.
source: o-Vanillin modulated gene expression of 40 genes including upregulation of cell cycle genes such as CDK6, CDK2C, CDK2D, and CDC25c while expression levels of CDK2A, Cyclin A2, Cyclin D1 and CCNB1 were decreased.
evidence: This is supported by gene expression analysis data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The data support the mechanistic action of RG-7112 to stabilize p53 and p21 by attenuating the MDM2-p53 interaction.
source: Collectively, the data support the mechanistic action of RG-7112 to stabilize p53 and p21 by attenuating the MDM2-p53 interaction (Weber, 2010; Tovar et al., 2013; Henley and Dick, 2012; Che et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data and citations to Weber, 2010; Tovar et al., 2013; Henley and Dick, 2012; Che et al., 2020.

claim: RG-7112 confirms regulation of the RB–E2F1 pathway that releases E2F1 and activates genes involved in cell cycle regulation, DNA synthesis, and cell proliferation.
source: Also, it confirms regulation of the RB–E2F1 pathway that releases E2F1 and activates genes involved in cell cycle regulation, DNA synthesis, and cell proliferation (Andreeff et al., 2016; Xu et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data and citations to Andreeff et al., 2016 and Xu et al., 2018.

claim: o-Vanillin treatment affected multiple pathways suggesting that o-Vanillin eliminates senescent cells both by apoptosis and non-apoptotic means.
source: o-Vanillin treatment affected multiple pathways suggesting that o-Vanillin eliminates senescent cells both by apoptosis and non-apoptotic means.
evidence: This is inferred from gene expression data showing multiple pathways affected by o-Vanillin.

claim: p16 deletion in NP cells from mouse discs with induced degeneration upregulates the expression of cyclin-dependent kinases 4/6, phosphorylated retinoblastoma protein, and transcription factor E2F1/2.
source: Recently, p16 deletion in NP cells from mouse discs with induced degeneration was shown to also upregulate the expression of cyclin-dependent kinases 4/6, phosphorylated retinoblastoma protein, and transcription factor E2F1/2 (Che et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Che et al., 2020.

claim: Clinical trials with RG-7112 for cancer treatment were limited by the high incidence of hematological toxicities.
source: Clinical trials with RG-7112 for cancer treatment were limited by the high incidence of hematological toxicities (Ray-Coquard et al., 2012; Jung et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Ray-Coquard et al., 2012 and Jung et al., 2008.

claim: A lower concentration (5 μM) and short exposure time of RG-7112 may prevent hematological side effects in patients treated for IVD degeneration.
source: Here, we used a lower concentration (5 μM) and short exposure time of RG-7112, in contrast to the high and toxic doses used in cancer therapy (20–1400 mg/m2 administrated daily for 10 days). This may prevent these side effects in patients treated for IVD degeneration.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the use of lower doses compared to cancer therapy.

claim: An administered dose of 4 mg UBX0101 was safe and well-tolerated, and it improved pain scores, reduced SASP factors and disease-related biomarkers after a single dose in patients with painful osteoarthritis of the knee.
source: This hypothesis was verified by the clinical study of the RG-7112 analogue UBX0101 in patients diagnosed with painful osteoarthritis of the knee. An administered dose of 4 mg was safe and well-tolerated, and it improved pain scores, reduced SASP factors and disease-related biomarkers after a single dose (Weber, 2010; Laberge et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Weber, 2010 and Laberge et al., 2018.

claim: The activation of multiple pathways following o-Vanillin treatment implies that diverse biological processes are affected.
source: The activation of multiple pathways following o-Vanillin treatment and within the selected set of 91 genes implies that diverse biological processes are affected, which was also reported for other natural senolytics like Quercetin, Fisetin, and Dasatinib (Pezet and McMahon, 2006; Wang et al., 2008).
evidence: This is inferred from gene expression data and supported by citations to Pezet and McMahon, 2006 and Wang et al., 2008.

claim: The activation of several mechanisms increases the capacity of natural senolytics to target the heterogeneous cellular states acquired by senescent cells after the initial growth arrest.
source: Although it is difficult to determine how these natural senolytics eliminate senescent cells and drive their therapeutic effects, the activation of several mechanisms increases their capacity to target the heterogeneous cellular states acquired by senescent cells after the initial growth arrest (Frolov and Dyson, 2004).
evidence: This is inferred from the data and supported by a citation to Frolov and Dyson, 2004.

claim: An antiinflammatory effect was expected for o-Vanillin from previous studies.

claim: This study documents, for the first time, antiinflammatory properties of RG-7112 in human IVD cells.
source: However, our study documents, for the first time, antiinflammatory properties of RG-7112 in human IVD cells.
evidence: This is supported by cytokine array and Luminex data showing decreased SASP factors.

claim: RG-7112 significantly reduced the concentrations of IFN-γ, IL-6 and CCL24 in pellet culture media.

evidence: This is established scientific knowledge.

claim: CCL7 expression has been reported to be concordant with IVD degeneration.

evidence: This is supported by citations to Binch et al., 2014 and Burke et al., 2002.

claim: The decrease of VEGF-A indicates a possible role of o-Vanillin to block the mechanism of neovascularization.

evidence: This is inferred from the data showing decreased VEGF-A levels.

evidence: This is supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: Animal models that replicate human disc pathology are limited due to the differences in anatomy, disc size, cell type, and loading.

evidence: This is supported by a citation to Jin et al., 2018.

claim: Notochord cells are retained longer in the majority of animal species.

evidence: This is supported by a citation to Grezella et al., 2018.

claim: Treatment with senolytics could increase proteoglycan content in human patients.
source: When comparing the intensity in RG-7112 and o-Vanillin-treated IVDs, we observed an increased intensity post-treatment, while a decrease was observed in vehicle-treated control. This suggests that treatment with senolytics could increase proteoglycan content in human patients.
evidence: This is inferred from MRI data showing increased T1ρ values in treated discs.

claim: Both RG-7112 and o-Vanillin significantly reduced the number of p16Ink4a-positive cells in treated intact discs.

evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: A slight but non-significant increase in proliferating cells was observed following senolytic treatment in intact discs.
source: Moreover, we observed a slight but non-significant increase in proliferating cells.
evidence: This is supported by Ki-67 immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: The findings correlate with the negative impact previously reported between the number of senescent cells and cell proliferation during IVD degeneration.
source: These findings correlate with the negative impact previously reported between the number of senescent cells and cell proliferation during IVD degeneration (Hwang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Hwang et al., 2018.

source: Furthermore, culture media from control discs, showed no change in cytokine release whereas both compounds decreased levels of IL-6, IL-7, IL-8, CXCL1, CXCL6, CCL2, CCL22, GROa/b/g, IGFBP-2, TNSF-14 and OPN.

evidence: This is supported by Luminex data from pellet and disc cultures.

evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the broader effects of o-Vanillin.

evidence: This is supported by data and citations to previous studies.

evidence: This is inferred from the combined in vitro and ex vivo data showing senolytic effects and matrix improvement.

evidence: This is speculative reasoning about the broader implications of the study.

claim: 91 of the 96 selected cellular senescence genes were expressed at a detectable level in human disc cells.
source: Gene expression analysis of 96 selected cellular senescence genes was performed and 91 of the 96 genes were expressed at a detectable level.
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data.

claim: Of the 91 genes identified, 44 were differentially expressed with a p<0.05 in one or both treatments.
source: Of the 91 genes identified, 44 were differentially expressed with a p<0.05 in one or both treatments (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by gene expression analysis data shown in Figure 2B.

source: Cell-cycle arrest of senescent disc cells is mainly mediated by the two pathways: p53-p21-Rb and p16-Rb.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge.
